disclaimer: MODELED values are transparent engineering judgments mapped from OBSERVED claims. Capacity expansion, strategic importance, order growth, and supplier concentration alone are not treated as proof of current scarcity. Generation queues are not load queues. 2028–2030 OEM expansions are capacity_growth, not present relief.

observations.demand_pressure_rationale: Siemens: transformer business including data-center projects was the major Grid Technologies order driver; GEV Electrification DC orders >$5B YTD. LPTs sit on both load and generation paths.
observations.capacity_pressure_rationale: Siemens GT book-to-bill 1.48 and €51B backlog show shipments trailing bookings. +50% capacity is a 2030 plan, not 2026 output. Week-level 2025/26 lead times remain secondary, so pressure is high but not maxed.
observations.capacity_growth_rationale: Siemens reports brownfield expansions already lifting shipments, with the large step-up targeted by 2030. Growth is real and late.
observations.supplier_concentration_rationale: Few global LPT/GSU OEMs (Siemens Energy, Hitachi Energy, GE Vernova class). Concentration is structural, not a 2026-only finding.
observations.lead_time_pressure_rationale: GAO 2023: large-utility LPT lead times 18–36 months vs 12–18 prior. Secondary 2025 surveys still show multi-year LPTs/GSUs. Not scored as 0.95 because current week counts are not primary.
observations.yield_risk_rationale: Custom LPT manufacturing has execution/test risk, but public evidence is lead time and backlog more than disclosed factory yield failure.
observations.technology_maturity_rationale: LPT technology is mature; the constraint is manufacturing slots and materials, not invention.
observations.qualification_difficulty_rationale: Units are custom-specified; a second source is not a drop-in spare across voltage classes.
observations.substitution_difficulty_rationale: No practical substitute for high-voltage transformation. Behind-the-meter generation still needs GSU transformers.
observations.geographic_concentration_rationale: Specialized plants are limited globally; U.S. expansions are announced but not yet the bulk of 2026 output.
observations.downstream_importance_rationale: Without LPTs/GSUs, neither grid energization nor new generation interconnection can complete.
observations.evidence_confidence_rationale: Primary 2026 backlog/BtB and 2023 GAO lead times are strong; precise 2026 week-level scarcity is still secondary.

observations.demand_pressure_rationale: PJM data-center load adjustments plus LBNL’s still-large active queue show intense pressure to connect new resources and, separately, large loads.
observations.capacity_pressure_rationale: Median IR-to-COD over five years for 2025 completions. Active queue still ~2,061 GW. This measures generation interconnection capacity of the process, not a datacenter load-queue census.
observations.capacity_growth_rationale: FERC Order 2023 / cluster reforms exist; LBNL still shows long COD times. Reform is not yet proven as restored throughput.
observations.supplier_concentration_rationale: A project faces a single ISO/RTO or utility process. Regional monopoly of process, not a single private OEM.
observations.lead_time_pressure_rationale: Observed multi-year IR-to-COD. Secondary PJM reporting that post-ISA time can exceed study time is treated as triangulation only.
observations.yield_risk_rationale: LBNL: only 13% of 2000–2020 requests reached COD by end-2025; most withdraw. Process completion risk is high.
observations.technology_maturity_rationale: Study processes are mature institutions; software/cluster reforms are the change, not new physics.
observations.qualification_difficulty_rationale: Each project still requires case-specific studies and upgrade cost assignment.
observations.substitution_difficulty_rationale: Behind-the-meter gas and surplus interconnection exist but are themselves equipment- and permit-constrained. Not a free substitute.
observations.geographic_concentration_rationale: Worst in specific ISO footprints (PJM, CAISO, etc.); ERCOT large-load process differs. Not a single national queue.
observations.downstream_importance_rationale: No interconnection, no energized campus on the grid path.
observations.evidence_confidence_rationale: LBNL is excellent primary for generation queues. Datacenter load interconnection is less directly measured here.

observations.demand_pressure_rationale: GEV 116 GW equipment+slots vs ~20 GW annual output is intense turbine demand. Secondary: only ~20% of that book is datacenter/AI — do not treat the whole backlog as AI load.
observations.capacity_pressure_rationale: Primary GEV: 116 GW under contract vs 20 GW 2026 run-rate; 24 GW is 2028 and 30 GW is 2030. That is a measured slot shortage for turbines, not inferred from expansion talk.
observations.capacity_growth_rationale: GEV is raising output 20→24→30 GW inside existing plants. Growth is committed and late relative to the booked queue.
observations.supplier_concentration_rationale: Heavy-duty frames concentrated in GE Vernova, Siemens Energy, and Mitsubishi Power.
observations.lead_time_pressure_rationale: Primary backlog/output ratio implies multi-year wait. Secondary call commentary of 2031 reservations supports, not independently required.
observations.yield_risk_rationale: These are known products shipping at 20 GW annualized; constraint is slots, not disclosed inability to build a turbine.
observations.technology_maturity_rationale: HA-class and peer frames are mature commercial products.
observations.qualification_difficulty_rationale: Plant wrapping, emissions, and interconnection still take years even after a slot is held.
observations.substitution_difficulty_rationale: Grid power is the substitute. That path is also slow. Smaller aero-derivatives exist but do not trivially replace HA-class GW campuses.
observations.geographic_concentration_rationale: Few large factories (e.g. Greenville) dominate heavy-duty output.
observations.downstream_importance_rationale: Binds the onsite/new-generation relief path. Not every campus needs a new turbine if grid headroom and interconnection exist.
observations.evidence_confidence_rationale: Primary quantified backlog vs output. DC share of the book is secondary, so DC-specific importance is not scored as if 100% of 116 GW were AI.

observations.demand_pressure_rationale: 549 GW already has an IA and is not operating — those projects still need physical transmission/substation work, often overlapping LPT demand.
observations.capacity_pressure_rationale: Post-ISA non-operation is observed. How much is transformers vs crews vs permitting is not fully separable in primary data, so pressure is high-moderate not extreme.
observations.capacity_growth_rationale: Utilities are expanding workplans; no primary evidence of a step-function in U.S. transmission construction productivity.
observations.supplier_concentration_rationale: Many EPCs and utilities, but specialized HV construction capacity is not infinite in AI-heavy zones.
observations.lead_time_pressure_rationale: IR-to-COD >5 years includes this construction interval. Secondary PJM ~4 years post-ISA is not treated as primary.
observations.yield_risk_rationale: Rights-of-way, outage windows, and upgrade restudies create completion risk.
observations.qualification_difficulty_rationale: Utility standards and commissioning remain project-specific.
observations.substitution_difficulty_rationale: Hard to energize a large load without the assigned upgrades; BTM generation can reduce some upgrade scope.
observations.geographic_concentration_rationale: Local to the interconnecting zone rather than a single factory geography.
observations.downstream_importance_rationale: After an ISA, this is the remaining physical path to COD for grid-connected projects.
observations.evidence_confidence_rationale: 549 GW with IA not COD is primary. Attribution among equipment vs construction vs permitting is partly modeled.

observations.demand_pressure_rationale: Eaton Electrical Americas DC orders ~+240% with revenue +50%; GEV Electrification DC orders >$5B YTD. Demand is primary and steep.
observations.capacity_pressure_rationale: Book-to-bill 1.2 and rising backlog show tightness, but Eaton is also delivering record sales. Order growth is not scored as LPT-class inability to supply.
observations.capacity_growth_rationale: Eaton is adding plants (including switchgear) and growing organic electrical sales in the mid-teens to 20% range.
observations.supplier_concentration_rationale: Several large electrical OEMs (Eaton, Siemens, Schneider, ABB, GEV). Less concentrated than heavy-duty turbines or LPTs.
observations.lead_time_pressure_rationale: Backlog growth implies waits, but primary filings here do not publish 2–4 year LPT-style lead times for switchgear.
observations.yield_risk_rationale: Standard industrial products; public constraint is demand/backlog more than yield collapse.
observations.technology_maturity_rationale: MV/HV switchgear is mature; data-center density is pulling more of the same plus some new architectures.
observations.qualification_difficulty_rationale: Hyperscaler specs and listing/testing add time but second sources exist.
observations.substitution_difficulty_rationale: Multiple OEMs can supply similar gear with requalification. Not a unique physics bottleneck.
observations.geographic_concentration_rationale: Manufacturing is multi-region; U.S. expansions underway.
observations.downstream_importance_rationale: Required to move power from the fence into halls, but usually after/alongside transformers.
observations.evidence_confidence_rationale: Primary Eaton/GEV demand is excellent. Scarcity magnitude is inferred from backlog, not from published multi-year lead times.

observations.demand_pressure_rationale: PJM 10-year summer growth 3.6%/year vs 0.3% in 2021, with many zones adjusted for data centers. Microsoft describes power as the binding shortage vs chips.
observations.capacity_pressure_rationale: Forecasted peak growth is not a measured 2026 blackout. Near-term PJM peaks were revised down after vetting large-load requests — announced MW ≠ certain load.
observations.capacity_growth_rationale: New generation COD remains slow (LBNL). Turbine slots for new plants are sold years out.
observations.supplier_concentration_rationale: Many generators, but spare capacity is local to constrained zones.
observations.lead_time_pressure_rationale: Adding headroom means new plants or transmission; both are multi-year.
observations.yield_risk_rationale: Forecast error (loads that never show) is a real risk in both directions.
observations.technology_maturity_rationale: The grid already operates; the issue is surplus in the right place at the right time.
observations.qualification_difficulty_rationale: Capacity market and resource-adequacy rules are institutional, not a factory qualification wall.
observations.substitution_difficulty_rationale: BTM generation, storage, and flexible load help but do not erase regional energy needs at GW scale.
observations.geographic_concentration_rationale: Tightness is zonal (AEP, DOM, etc.), not uniform nationally.
observations.downstream_importance_rationale: Without energy/capacity, an interconnection agreement does not create operating AI load.
observations.evidence_confidence_rationale: PJM forecast and Microsoft power language are primary. Present-year reserve tightness is modeled from those, not from a 2026 adequacy filing excerpted here.

observations.demand_pressure_rationale: Every large campus and new generator needs entitlements; AI siting volume is high in a few counties.
observations.capacity_pressure_rationale: Secondary PJM milestone mix (29% permitting) suggests delay contribution. Not treated as a measured national permit shortage.
observations.capacity_growth_rationale: Local processes do not scale like factories; little evidence of systematic acceleration.
observations.supplier_concentration_rationale: Thousands of jurisdictions; concentration is political/local, not OEM.
observations.lead_time_pressure_rationale: Siting can add years, but primary national statistics in this dataset are thin.
observations.yield_risk_rationale: Projects can be denied or litigated to death; binary kill risk is real.
observations.technology_maturity_rationale: Legal process, not a technology readiness issue.
observations.qualification_difficulty_rationale: Environmental and land-use reviews are sequential and appealable.
observations.substitution_difficulty_rationale: Brownfield and existing generating sites help; moving a GW campus is still costly.
observations.geographic_concentration_rationale: Hotspots (Northern Virginia, parts of Ohio, Texas) matter more than a national average.
observations.downstream_importance_rationale: Can halt a project regardless of equipment orders.
observations.evidence_confidence_rationale: Weakest evidence node: one secondary citation of PJM milestone shares. Scored below equipment nodes on purpose.

observations.demand_pressure_rationale: Microsoft: short space or power to install GPUs; using long-lived leases. Demand for halls is real.
observations.capacity_pressure_rationale: Space is co-stated with power. Construction can often proceed while waiting on energization. Do not score shells as the scarce input without evidence that empty powered halls are plentiful.
observations.capacity_growth_rationale: Hyperscaler capex and colocation build are expanding rapidly; Microsoft is leasing as well as building.
observations.supplier_concentration_rationale: Many GCs and developers; not an OEM bottleneck.
observations.lead_time_pressure_rationale: Buildings take time, but typically less than multi-year LPT/turbine/interconnection clocks when land is entitled.
observations.yield_risk_rationale: Ordinary construction execution risk, not a unique AI failure mode in the evidence base.
observations.technology_maturity_rationale: Shell construction is mature; liquid-cooled high-density design is the newer piece (scored on the cooling node).
observations.qualification_difficulty_rationale: Hyperscaler design standards exist; many builders can meet them.
observations.substitution_difficulty_rationale: Lease vs build, multiple markets. Powered land is the hard part.
observations.geographic_concentration_rationale: Clustered in power-available markets, which is circular with the power nodes.
observations.downstream_importance_rationale: No hall, no deployment — but a dark hall without power also fails.
observations.evidence_confidence_rationale: Primary Microsoft space/power language. Construction-industry scarcity metrics are not in this dataset.

observations.demand_pressure_rationale: Vertiv: AI and general compute demand intensifying; Eaton bought Boyd Thermal. Density is pulling liquid cooling.
observations.capacity_pressure_rationale: Vertiv describes temporary congestion and still raised full-year guidance. That is execution strain, not a proven industry-wide cooling shortage that stops energization.
observations.capacity_growth_rationale: Vertiv is accelerating capacity expansion and acquisitions; cooling vendors are investing.
observations.supplier_concentration_rationale: Several scaled vendors (Vertiv, Schneider, Eaton/Boyd). More contestable than turbines/LPTs.
observations.lead_time_pressure_rationale: Primary filing does not publish multi-year CDU lead times; secondary 6–10 month figures are not used to max this score.
observations.yield_risk_rationale: Complex multi-phase deployments create timing risk (Vertiv). Not a fab-yield story.
observations.technology_maturity_rationale: Liquid cooling is shipping at scale but still a transition from air for many halls.
observations.qualification_difficulty_rationale: Facility integration and fluid quality are non-trivial; still faster to dual-source than LPTs.
observations.substitution_difficulty_rationale: Lower-density air cooling is a partial substitute that leaves performance on the table.
observations.geographic_concentration_rationale: Global manufacturing; not a single-country chokepoint in this evidence set.
observations.downstream_importance_rationale: Required for high-density racks, but a campus can still be power-blocked first.
observations.evidence_confidence_rationale: Primary Vertiv demand/congestion. Congestion explicitly framed as temporary; do not promote to #1.

observations.demand_pressure_rationale: AI accelerator demand remains the load driver. This X-Ray tests whether that demand currently binds physical expansion.
observations.capacity_pressure_rationale: RED CELL: Microsoft stated it was not short GPUs/CPUs but short space or power, with chips waiting on infrastructure. Do not rank compute as the datacenter-buildout bottleneck on 2026 hyperscaler testimony.
observations.capacity_growth_rationale: Accelerator supply continues to ramp (see AI Accelerator X-Ray for packaging/HBM). Not re-scored here as the binding plant constraint.
observations.supplier_concentration_rationale: GPU/custom ASIC supply remains concentrated. Concentration ≠ current DC expansion bind.
observations.lead_time_pressure_rationale: Lead times exist, but the cited hyperscaler constraint is inability to plug chips in, not inability to obtain them.
observations.yield_risk_rationale: Packaging/HBM yield is a semiconductor issue covered in the other X-Ray, not this infrastructure model.
observations.technology_maturity_rationale: Deployable products exist at volume; the hall/power path is the gating item in the testimony used here.
observations.qualification_difficulty_rationale: Platform qualification is real but is not what Microsoft described as the shortage.
observations.substitution_difficulty_rationale: Limited alternative accelerators at the frontier, irrelevant if the hall has no power.
observations.geographic_concentration_rationale: Advanced packaging/foundry geography is concentrated (see AI Accelerator X-Ray).
observations.downstream_importance_rationale: The economic purpose of the campus. Importance is not scarcity.
observations.evidence_confidence_rationale: Direct primary hyperscaler statement that compute hardware was not the constraint.
